svg.title: Four methods, computed
svg.desc: Four methods, computed with setuhq.methods (the functions the app's Methods chapters draw with and the tests check). 1. Transit with limb darkening (transit_flux): pi Men c, k = Rp/R★ = 0.0156 from exoplanet.eu's 0.16719 RJ and 1.1 R☉ star, b = 0.5738, quadratic limb darkening u1 = 0.333, u2 = 0.228 (Claret 2017, Teff 6037 K): depth 267 ppm, against 244 ppm for a uniform disc, plotted against the planet's position across the star in stellar radii. 2. Radial velocity (rv_curve): HD 80606 b, P = 111.44 d, e = 0.93183, ω = 301.213°, K = 469.22 m/s, over one orbit. 3. Microlensing (paczynski): point-lens magnification A(u), on a log scale, against time in Einstein-crossing times for u0 = 0.1: peak A = 10.04, u0 = 0.3: peak A = 3.44, u0 = 1: peak A = 1.34. 4. Blocking starlight (airy_intensity, lyot_final_intensity): the star's image against separation 0 to 12 λ/D on a log scale, for a clear pupil and a Lyot coronagraph with a 4 λ/D mask; at 8 λ/D the clear pupil leaves 7.8×10⁻⁵ of the peak, the Lyot stop at 150% 6.7×10⁻⁵ and at 80% 1.8×10⁻⁷. Axes: relative flux against position across the star in stellar radii; radial velocity in m/s, with zero marked, against orbital phase; magnification on a log scale against time in Einstein-crossing times; intensity relative to the unblocked peak on a log scale against separation in λ/D. Models from stored values, not observations. Sources: src/setuhq/methods.py and docs/results/methods_examples.json (exoplanet.eu, fetched 2026-10-18), commit 77360d6.
